evidence_status: Design recommendations and source-linked candidate notes supplied by coordinator; no candidates installed or locally verified.

candidate_comparison.name: Open-LLM-VTuber
candidate_comparison.fit: Coordinator recommendation: start with Windows desktop-pet interaction and a Japanese Nino TTS MVP. A Python text-to-WAV adapter appears close to the existing local CLI boundary.
candidate_comparison.integration_note: Connect generated Japanese spoken text to existing local TTS; keep subtitles/captions for Chinese explanation separate from spoken text. Do not claim native Irodori support without an adapter.

candidate_comparison.name: AIRI
candidate_comparison.fit: Coordinator recommendation for a fuller 2D/3D and mouth-motion path after the first MVP.

candidate_comparison.name: N.E.K.O
candidate_comparison.repo_snapshot: Coordinator reports approximately 3.1k GitHub stars as a page estimate on 2026-11-01, not an API-verified count.
candidate_comparison.fit: Python 3.11/FastAPI services with an Electron host; docs describe Main, Memory, and Agent services, multi-window frontend options including Live2D/VRM/MMD/PNGTuber, and a TTS worker queue with WebSocket audio and interruption queue handling.
candidate_comparison.integration_note: The documented TTS worker interface includes request/response queues, API key and voice ID, and 48 kHz mono PCM16 with speech IDs. GPT-SoVITS/vLLM-Omni providers are cited; Irodori is not listed. A custom provider/adapter would be required. More services mean higher integration cost than a speech-first prototype.

candidate_comparison.name: Mate-Engine
candidate_comparison.repo_snapshot: Coordinator reports approximately 3.8k GitHub stars as a page estimate on 2026-11-01, not an API-verified count.
candidate_comparison.fit: Unity Windows VRM desktop pet features are described as window/taskbar sitting, dragging, idle behavior, and eye/head tracking. README comparison indicates AI Chat, while AI Voices is absent.
candidate_comparison.integration_note: TTS and character-agent behavior still need implementation. License file is described as mixed MateEnginePro v2.1/AGPL terms and separate asset terms; do not summarize it as permissive MIT.

candidate_comparison.name: VPet
candidate_comparison.fit: Useful as a 2D sprite pet/interaction reference; not a complete Japanese voice agent by itself.

candidate_comparison.name: BongoCat
candidate_comparison.fit: Useful as an event/Live2D interaction reference; not a complete voice agent by itself.

recommended_design.first_host: Evaluate Open-LLM-VTuber as the first Windows desktop-pet host, with a Python adapter from Japanese text to local Irodori WAV generation.
recommended_design.later_options: Consider AIRI for a more complete 2D/3D and lip-sync experience; consider N.E.K.O for proactive companionship and persistent memory; consider Mate-Engine if a 3D VRM pet becomes the priority.
recommended_design.streaming_framing: For MVP, split a complete Japanese reply into short sentences, generate the next while playing the previous. This sentence-level pipeline can improve perceived responsiveness but does not establish native Irodori audio streaming. Do not call a whole-WAV HTTP wrapper true model streaming.
recommended_design.resource_framing: On the known 4 GB GPU/16 GB RAM machine, prioritize local TTS and a light avatar. The LLM may run in a lab/server or through another provider. Do not assume the LLM, ASR, TTS, and avatar all fit together in local GPU/RAM budgets. Run inference through one resident worker with a controlled queue; frontend sentence pipelining must not launch parallel Irodori model instances on 4 GB VRAM.
recommended_design.watermark_framing: Retain the existing Irodori watermark processing contract in the normal output path and include its measured CPU latency in response planning; do not silently remove it.
recommended_design.language_framing: Nino spoken text is Japanese. Chinese subtitles may explain the content; captions should not be spoken aloud.
recommended_design.stop_cancel_framing: Player stop can immediately clear queued playback and suppress late audio by request_id. True inference cancellation requires runtime cooperation and is a separate capability; do not conflate the two.
recommended_design.visual_asset_framing: No usable Nino-specific visual asset is evidenced in the workspace. Live2D is not a settled requirement; a two-mouth-state PNG prototype can validate basic speech animation while assets are sourced.

stages.name: Typed dialogue MVP
stages.scope: Agent produces Japanese spoken text plus attitude/intensity/delivery; local TTS; transparent desktop avatar with simple mouth motion and expression. Use a single resident inference worker with a bounded queue; validate a two-mouth PNG prototype if no suitable character asset is available.
stages.acceptance: Type a turn, receive Japanese speech, play it through a queue, and display an avatar response. Report first-playable-audio separately from full-file synthesis and cold start.

stages.name: Voice input and continuity
stages.scope: Microphone, VAD/ASR, stop/cancel behavior, short-term context, persistent memory. Separate immediate playback stop and stale request suppression from runtime-cooperative inference cancellation; add Japanese date/time/number/name reading normalization.
stages.acceptance: Voice turn is detected, current speech can be cancelled, stale queued audio is dropped, and approved memory can be retrieved after restart. Demonstrate playback queue clear and stale request_id suppression independently of runtime generation cancellation; verify Japanese date/time/number/person-name reading examples.

stages.name: Richer desktop interaction
stages.scope: Head pats, dragging, time-based events, proactive dialogue, optional screen context, fuller animation.
stages.acceptance: Each optional interaction has an explicit opt-in and observable behavior; animation and speech remain responsive together.

integration_gaps: Nino-specific visual assets, expressions, and motion are not evidenced in the current workspace.
Windows transparent topmost window, click-through, dragging, tray controls, and desktop input integration.
Japanese character dialogue policy, role definition, short-term context, and persistent memory; source provenance for official versus community character settings.
Resident local TTS process, short-sentence pipeline, caching, cancellation, and playback queue.
Audio-driven mouth motion and emotion-linked expression animation.
Microphone VAD/ASR, echo handling, and barge-in cancellation.
Windows startup, packaging, and measured resource coexistence with avatar and other providers.
Single resident inference worker and bounded request queue; sentence pipelining must reuse the worker rather than start parallel Irodori model instances on 4 GB VRAM.
Separate immediate playback stop/queue clearing and stale request_id suppression from cooperative cancellation of active model inference.
Japanese text normalization for date, time, number, and person-name readings; pronunciation has been a user-reported issue and needs explicit test examples during implementation.
Nino-specific usable visual asset is not evidenced; choose Live2D later or prototype two PNG mouth states first.
